decisions.reason: As a newly launched dietary supplement range with its own page and clear fit to the firm's portfolio-broadening strategy, it is still a low-cost option worth keeping while demand becomes clearer.

The product received dedicated launch promotion and supports the firm's consumer-health expansion, so management would likely keep it on the market because uncertainty remains high and the cost of waiting for better evidence is modest.

Although it appears less prominently than A and B, it is a recent adjacent OTC launch and the firm is large, expanding, and inclined to preserve such options until market acceptance is better revealed.

This is the most niche and least prominently presented supplement, which raises abandonment risk somewhat, but as a recent low-commitment portfolio option it is still more likely to be kept for further learning than dropped immediately.

The valsartan-related issue increases the chance of withdrawal, but because generics are core to the firm's business and quality or supply problems can often be remedied, management would more likely try to retain this option than exit within the next year.
